review_policy: Provisional assistant source/normative assessment, not owner approval or a conformance certificate. Source hashes bind the review. Functional contracts relate implementation to project models; translation from T.88 and T.6 remains a separate review obligation. Feature worklists are not exhaustive requirement counts.

remaining_scope: Complete segment syntax, payload dispatch and decoder-wide normative enumeration remain open; selected helper contracts do not prove parser output fields.
Encoder requirements are excluded only because support-matrix policy explicitly defers encoding.
Complete header-to-body dispatch, document lifecycle and rejection completeness remain unenumerated or unproved.
Complete D.1 enumeration and byte-to-returned-segment ordering/layout contracts remain open; EOF and lifecycle interactions need separate review.
Complete D.2 enumeration, rejection completeness and returned header/payload correspondence contracts remain open.
Embedding-container order/reassembly responsibilities and complete D.3 enumeration remain open; no PDF-container semantics are claimed.

These are explicitly project API-policy records, not PDF container requirements. Global/page reassembly, lifetime and output equivalence remain open; no approved PDF-container normative source has been consulted.

Complete page information and lifecycle enumeration remains open. Raw dimension/resolution-to-output relations, page initialization pixels, limit-policy separation and completion require independent proofs/review.
Sentinel parsing and exact rejection completeness remain unproved; full unknown-height page/stripe lifecycle, allocation strategy and output correspondence are not exhaustively enumerated.
Complete arithmetic initialization, renormalization, byte input, transition, integer and IAID obligations remain open; decision equivalence is not proved.
Independent per-table normative review and complete table/caller selection enumeration remain open; prefix selection and whole-decoder value equivalence are unproved.

Complete B.2/B.3 enumeration, encoded-table output relation, canonical prefix assignment theorem and caller selection remain open; shared B.4 helper evidence is recorded under standard_huffman_tables, not independently duplicated here.

Selected approved-source T.6 mode/run/framing records are present, not a complete T.6 enumeration. Independent table/geometry review, actual prefix-bit matching, run sums, line/raster pixels and caller propagation remain unproved. Apply T.88 6.2.6 exceptions explicitly; padding, optional EOFB and extension applicability need source-specific review. Typed errors are separately bound project API policy, not fabricated T.6 error requirements.
Remaining template geometry, skip/typical prediction timing, first-row behavior and complete generic raster semantics need decomposition and review.
Diagram-to-gather-order review, adaptive/reference alignment, edge pixels, prediction timing, arithmetic state and complete refinement raster/reference selection semantics remain open.

Remaining flags/table selection, imports, height/width recurrences, collective/direct/refined bitmap semantics, export-run interpretation and context save/restore still need complete decomposition and output proofs.

Full flag fields, strip-delta recurrences, entropy/ID consumption, instance order, refinement selection and composed visible pixels remain open; a current-state placement theorem is not a whole text-region theorem.
Complete header/flag and generic-parameter enumeration, collective bitmap decoding and per-pattern count/order/pixel extraction theorems remain open.

Complete header/parameter and bitplane enumeration, full mask/index values, pattern lookup, pixel combination and row-major rendering semantics remain open despite exact grid/depth/boundary helper contracts.

Visible page composition, direct/refinement distinctions, lossless-type constraints and complete dispatch/caller propagation remain open. Sealed-stripe guard evidence does not prove all page-write bounds.
Buffer bitmap identity, non-page-effect theorem, refinement reassociation, lifetime/discard rules and complete type/caller dispatch remain open.

Aggregation instance-count decoding, single-versus-multiple dispatch, Table 17 parameter propagation and aggregate bitmap outputs remain open; shared text-refinement geometry does not prove the dictionary's count-one path.
Page identity, contiguous numbering, lifecycle, ordering and decoded output correspondence remain open beyond parsed page-count agreement.
Full allowed-type/reference scope, global import resolution, collisions and retention/lifetime semantics require complete enumeration and exported functional proofs.
Deferred non-retain/attached-extension semantics and complete lifetime transitions remain open; the 7.2.8 example conflict still requires owner adjudication.
Reference resolution, allowed types, cross-page scope, retention interaction and full graph/lifecycle semantics remain open.
Packed byte/word operator output contracts, full page/region field propagation, refinement-specific operator restrictions and complete composed-pixel semantics remain open.
Full striping-bit/max-size field enumeration, earlier-write/later-write constraints, exact lifecycle errors and decoded final-height propagation remain open.
These rows trace project-profile typed rejection, not T.88's colour decoding procedure. Complete colour declaration/segment detection and rejection proofs remain open; unsupported is not excluded.

This is a project prohibition contextualized by informative 0.2, not a newly invented normative clause. End-to-end encoded-symbol identity/refinement/rendering and independent no-substitution tests remain open.

requirements.title: Use an imaginary white reference line before decoding the first row
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Successful raster decoding returns valid bitmap/reader storage. The exported contract does not state the initial reference line or first-row pixels.
assumptions: T.6's first reference is a coding convention, not a claim that the first decoded image row is white; the linked white-row case observes one resulting path.
gaps: Prove initial white-reference transitions and their relation to the first row's mode interpretation and visible output pixels.

requirements.title: Use each completed decoded row as the following row's reference
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The raster's successful output is storage-valid, without an exported correspondence between saved reference transitions and the previously decoded row.
assumptions: Executable repeated-row examples exercise reference reuse; valid transition bounds are not an exact pixel-to-transition relation.
gaps: Prove completed-row transition extraction, reference replacement, row ordering and all subsequent row pixel semantics.

requirements.title: Locate bounded reference changing-element positions for mode decoding
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: For a valid ordered reference sequence and in-range cursor, successful positions satisfy x <= b1 <= b2 <= width and the saved search index remains in range.
assumptions: Reference-line validity is a precondition; the model's width sentinels do not independently identify the first required opposite-colour transition.
gaps: Review the changing-element geometry and prove exact b1/b2 selection, colour parity, initial-position convention and missing-element fallback.

tokens: Ok((b1, b2)) => x <= b1 <= b2 <= width

requirements.title: Advance a pass-mode coding position to the second reference changing element
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Raster storage validity is proved, not the pass-mode position update, emitted span values or correspondence to the reference elements.
assumptions: The mode and reference pair must already be correctly selected; runtime scan agreement is not a formal T.6 transition theorem.
gaps: Prove the pass position update, colour/span semantics, progress and subsequent mode interpretation against an independent line model.

requirements.title: Interpret vertical mode as a signed displacement from the first reference changing element
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Successful bitmap storage is valid; the contract does not relate decoded vertical displacement, emitted pixels or the changed coding colour.
assumptions: The base scheme has seven vertical choices. The selected raster examples cover zero and unit displacements, not every signed displacement/boundary combination.
gaps: Prove signed offset interpretation, endpoint/colour transitions and pixel spans for all vertical modes, including row-edge and invalid-transition behavior.

requirements.title: Dispatch the coding-mode prefix through the implementation mode table
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The reader remains valid and successful output has an implementation-table witness with matching mode and consumed length. The postcondition does not state that consumed bits equal that witness's prefix.
assumptions: mode_code_is_normative is a project table-membership predicate despite its name; the table-driven test alone is not an independently transcribed normative oracle.
gaps: Independently review all Table 1 entries, prove input-prefix matching/completeness and propagate returned modes into exact line transitions; extension applicability is separate.

requirements.title: Decode two successive opposite-colour runs after a horizontal mode
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Raster storage and run-reader validity are maintained; the exported contracts do not identify the ordered run pair or resulting horizontal pixel spans.
assumptions: Each selected run must use its proper colour table; bounded run totals do not establish correct paired consumption or coding-position updates.
gaps: Prove horizontal-prefix dispatch, run-colour order, both lengths, endpoint update and exact two-span pixel contents.

requirements.title: Look up a supplied white-run code key in the white/common implementation tables
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Some output belongs to the selected implementation arrays and has the supplied bits/length key. For this requirement black is false; the helper does not prove every defined key is found.
assumptions: The lookup key has already been gathered correctly. run_code_is_normative only means implementation-array membership, not independent faithfulness to the approved T.6 tables.
gaps: Review every white/common table entry independently, prove lookup completeness and bitstream-to-key equality, then decoded length and terminating/make-up semantics.

requirements.title: Look up a supplied black-run code key in the black/common implementation tables
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Some output is a matching-key member of the selected implementation arrays. For this requirement black is true; table contents and all defined-key acceptance are separate obligations.
assumptions: The same helper handles both colours, but their normative code assignments differ; shared common make-up entries do not imply the terminating arrays are interchangeable.
gaps: Independently review black/common entries and prove colour selection, lookup completeness, actual prefix consumption and code length/value interpretation.

requirements.title: Accumulate make-up lengths followed by a terminating run code
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The reader remains bounded and a successful total is no larger than remaining. No postcondition states that the total is the sum of decoded make-up and terminating lengths.
assumptions: The supplied remaining extent must be the correct row remainder; the two selected examples do not cover repeated long make-up sequences.
gaps: Prove summation, terminating-code completion and exact consumption; add independent repeated-long-make-up cases and all zero/limit boundaries.

requirements.title: Handle the imaginary initial white element and zero-length leading white run
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Valid output storage does not prove the initial imaginary-element position/colour or preservation of a zero-length leading run.
assumptions: The implementation's zero-based cursor convention must be related explicitly to T.6's imaginary element before the first actual pixel.
gaps: Prove initial-position equivalence, initial colour, zero-length-run treatment and progress without deleting meaningful same-position transitions.

requirements.title: Finish the reference representation with bounded width-position sentinels
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Given a valid full-width transition prefix, finishing adds two entries and establishes reference_line_valid, including two terminal width sentinels.
assumptions: Two stored sentinels are an implementation representation of missing reference elements, not a prescribed T.6 allocation layout.
gaps: Prove preservation of all prior transition entries, exact row pixel correspondence, last coding-element completion and caller use of the sentinels.

requirements.title: Recognize the T.6 end-of-facsimile-block marker when framing requires it
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Under Required policy, successful finishing implies exact_eofb at the old bit position and a final position at the bounded input's end.
assumptions: The project exact_eofb predicate reads a 24-bit marker; independent constant/model review remains required. T.88 permits omission in specified known-byte contexts, so Required applicability must not be inferred for every JBIG2 MMR invocation.
gaps: Prove caller framing policy, full acceptance/error conditions and propagation into returned block byte counts; preserve the separately mapped T.88 exceptions.

requirements.title: Check zero-valued padding in T.6 post-EOFB framing
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Finishing preserves reader validity and framing positions, but neither exported contract states that all consumed padding bits are zero.
assumptions: T.6 explicitly specifies zero-valued pad bits after EOFB and permits octet/fixed-block alignment. This record does not automatically settle how T.88's byte-boundary/known-extent exceptions apply to every prefix or optional-EOFB path.
gaps: Prove the actual padding bit values and exact errors; review T.88 applicability and fixed-block versus project octet-only trailing-data behavior before resolving the pending padding-policy question.

requirements.clause: 2.2.3.3; 2.2.4 (syntax context; typed error is project API policy)
requirements.title: Report truncated horizontal run input with a typed error while preserving bounded reader state
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The reader remains valid and input bytes are unchanged; the contract does not specify the exact UnexpectedEof variant or public error mapping.
assumptions: T.6 defines valid coding syntax, not this Rust error API. The support matrix's approved public API requires typed errors; the selected unit test observes the private MMR/reader error.
gaps: Prove exact typed failure, offset/colour fields, public DecodeError mapping, complete truncation detection and caller recovery; do not count this policy as another normative T.6 rule.

requirements.clause: 2.2.5.2 (line-extent context; typed error is project API policy)
requirements.title: Reject a run beyond the supplied row remainder with a typed error
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Reader validity and bounded successful totals are proved; the exact RunExceedsRow error, failure consumption and public mapping are not postconditions.
assumptions: The caller supplies the correct row remainder; typed malformed-input handling is approved project API policy, not a prescribed T.6 diagnostic.
gaps: Prove run-sum comparison, exact error classification/consumption and all caller-supplied row-bound relations.

requirements.clause: 2.4.1.1 (marker context; typed error is project API policy)
requirements.title: Report missing or truncated required EOFB with a typed framing error
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Reader validity is preserved by the framing helpers; neither contract identifies MissingEofb or proves complete failure classification for absent/truncated markers.
assumptions: The caller's Required/prefix framing policy is appropriate. T.88 Optional cases must not be reclassified as missing-marker errors merely from T.6 framing context.
gaps: Prove exact errors, consumed positions and public mapping for every required-framing truncation; review marker-versus-padding and optional-policy boundaries.

requirements.title: Derive the number of patterns from the maximum pattern index
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The helper equals pattern_count, whose definition is decoded gray_max plus one in an unbounded natural-number model.
assumptions: The maximum index has already been parsed; this count relation alone does not prove the header bytes or returned dictionary length.
gaps: Prove raw GRAYMAX extraction, output pattern count, index ordering and bounded caller conversion/allocation.

requirements.title: Compute collective pattern width as count times individual pattern width
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Some width is exactly the mathematical product and fits u32; None implies the product exceeds u32.
assumptions: Inputs must be the intended decoded count and width; machine representability and project memory limits are not normative pattern limits.
gaps: Propagate the derived count/width and common height into generic decoding and prove collective pixel contents and complete acceptance conditions.

tokens: width as nat == pattern_count as nat * pattern_width as nat
None => pattern_count as nat * pattern_width as nat > u32::MAX as nat

requirements.title: Extract consecutive equal-width patterns from the collective bitmap
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Successful extraction returns storage-valid pattern bitmaps and valid work state; exact pattern count, dimensions, sequence order and source pixels are not postconditions.
assumptions: Collective storage and work state are valid; the source may have byte/pixel offsets not aligned to pattern boundaries.
gaps: Prove output length, dimensions and each visible pattern pixel's collective source coordinate, including cross-byte boundaries.

requirements.title: Compute signed fixed-point pattern locations using the grid origin and vectors
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Fixed-point x/y equal their signed project formulas, and fixed_to_pixel equals the arithmetic-shift model.
assumptions: The parsed grid origin/vector and grid coordinates are supplied correctly; model-to-normative arithmetic translation requires independent review.
gaps: Prove signed header field interpretation and propagation into all skip/render calls and their row-major ordering.

tokens: out.0 as int == halftone_spec::grid_x_fixed(header, grid_x, grid_y)
out.1 as int == halftone_spec::grid_y_fixed(header, grid_x, grid_y)

requirements.title: Choose the minimum grayscale bit depth for the supplied pattern count
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Successful depth equals gray_depth_expected for a count in the representable one-through-2^32 domain; an error implies the count is outside it.
assumptions: The project depth model must be reviewed against the ceiling-log definition; the count must equal the selected dictionary's actual length.
gaps: Prove dictionary count propagation, complete success conditions and exact plane count/consumption in decode_gray_planes.

requirements.title: Reconstruct grayscale values from most-significant-first Gray-coded planes
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The executing bytewise XOR helper preserves current-plane storage and plane decoding preserves valid state/work. Neither contract promises reconstructed plane pixels or grayscale index values.
assumptions: The scalar Gray-bit helper used by a test oracle is not promoted into a functional theorem for the optimized bytewise runtime path.
gaps: Prove XOR values, most-significant plane order, index bit accumulation and complete coded-plane/returned-index correspondence.

requirements.title: Classify a pattern wholly outside the halftone region using half-open bounds
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The boundary helper equals wholly_outside, conditional on right/bottom being the exact signed coordinate-plus-pattern extents.
assumptions: The caller must supply those exact extents and the correct grid position; touching a region edge is intentionally distinguished from overlap.
gaps: Independently review the geometric predicate and prove that generate_skip_mask stores exactly this result for every grid cell.

tokens: out == halftone_spec::wholly_outside(x, y, pattern_width, pattern_height, region_width, region_height,)

requirements.title: Render selected patterns in grid order with clipped operator application
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The helper preserves destination storage, not clipped pattern pixel values, the selected pattern index or the caller's row-major iteration order.
assumptions: Pattern/destination storage is valid; determinism and bounded scalar agreement do not constitute a formal whole-halftone result.
gaps: Prove pattern lookup, exact clipped/operator pixels, outside frames and sequential overlap effects through decode_halftone_region.

requirements.title: Combine an immediate direct region bitmap into its page buffer
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The caller preserves storage validity of its page buffers. This is not a composed-pixel result or exact-source equivalence theorem for any called bitmap kernel.
assumptions: Consult the current audited inventory for transitive executing/proof-body substitutions in bitmap composition. The caller's storage contract does not independently discharge that boundary.
gaps: Prove page pixels/operator effects, caller region association and immediate-type dispatch; any remaining transitive exact-source boundary must be closed separately.

requirements.title: Restrict an immediate region's observable page effect to its page intersection
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The page caller preserves its bitmap storage. Runtime tests observe clipped pixels, but no caller postcondition specifies the page intersection, pixel values or exterior frame.
assumptions: This is a scoped finite-page effect, not permission to accept every geometry. Consult the current audited inventory for transitive kernel source substitutions; no removed scalar helper is used as exact-source evidence.
gaps: Prove exact clipped coordinates, composed pixels, unchanged outside pixels and acceptance/error boundaries, independently of caller storage validity.

requirements.title: Prevent a later intersecting region from writing at or above an already sealed stripe end row
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: For successful intersecting requests with a prior sealed row, region_y exceeds that row. Nonintersecting success preserves the prior open-stripe maximum marker.
assumptions: The caller supplies correct geometry and saved stripe state; this is a guard contract, not a theorem for all page pixel writes.
gaps: Prove caller propagation, exact error behavior and the complementary rule preventing earlier segments from modifying below a later stripe end row.

requirements.title: Retain an intermediate direct bitmap in auxiliary storage rather than draw it immediately
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Successful insertion preserves region_buffers_valid; it does not promise bitmap identity, buffer-key association or absence of page mutation by the entire dispatch path.
assumptions: Input buffers and the inserted bitmap are storage-valid; the generated black intermediate bitmap is observed not to alter a white final page.
gaps: Prove exact buffer contents/segment association and full dispatch non-page effect, then refinement reassociation and eventual discard/lifetime semantics.

requirements.title: Respect the page's declaration that auxiliary-buffer regions may occur
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The verified guard has no postcondition for auxiliary permission or its exact InvalidPageState rejection.
assumptions: The page flag has already been propagated into auxiliary_allowed; this requirement does not cover every segment that may require an auxiliary buffer.
gaps: Prove permission/rejection equivalence, raw page-flag propagation and complete guarded dispatch for all intermediate/refinement types.

requirements.title: Interpret the dictionary refinement/aggregation mode flag
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Successful dictionary_config_safe relates config.refinement_aggregation to input flag bit 1; it does not prove any downstream aggregation branch.
assumptions: The field is supplied as a parsed flag word; the standard distinguishes direct-coded and refinement/aggregate-coded symbol paths.
gaps: Prove field extraction, instance-count decoding, count-one/count-many dispatch and all aggregation parameter/output relations.

requirements.title: Compute shared text-refinement dimensions and floor-half reference offsets
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Successful geometry uses base-plus-delta dimensions and floor-half(delta)+offset reference displacement, with project dimension bounds.
assumptions: This is the shared text-refinement geometry relevant to multi-instance aggregation; the dictionary's count-one path has different parameters and is not established here.
gaps: Review Table 12/model arithmetic and prove Table 17 caller propagation, count-dependent dispatch and actual refined/aggregate pixels.

tokens: geometry.width as int == base_width as int + delta_width as int
geometry.height as int == base_height as int + delta_height as int
geometry.reference_dx as int == symbol_text_spec::floor_half(delta_width as int) + delta_x as int
geometry.reference_dy as int == symbol_text_spec::floor_half(delta_height as int) + delta_y as int

requirements.title: Distinguish permitted page-independent resources from segment types that require a page
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The association validator is verified for safety without a postcondition characterizing allowed page-zero types.
assumptions: T.88 page-independent association is not itself a PDF global-container definition; the project API supplies that reuse policy separately.
gaps: Prove exact allowed-type/page-association conditions and all typed rejection cases, including EOF association and every region/boundary type.

requirements.title: Forbid page-independent resources from referring to page-scoped segments
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The helper verifies bounded index use conditional on valid index entries, but exports no complete scope/resolution postcondition.
assumptions: The generated case uses dictionary resources and a real page-associated target; target existence and lifetime are separate constraints.
gaps: Prove page-zero/same-page/cross-page reference rules, successful global import lookup, complete errors and interaction with allowed reference types.

requirements.title: Apply the five combination operators to two binary pixel values
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: The Boolean helper equals the project combine model for its two pixel inputs and operator.
assumptions: Boolean truth-table correctness does not establish the packed-byte/chunk implementations or every raster caller.
gaps: Review the model independently and prove packed operator values and composition through clipping, frame and page-state relations.

requirements.title: Interpret recognized wire combination-operator codes with context-specific Replace permission
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Success matches the local encoded-code/Replace-permission model; errors imply no permitted model entry.
assumptions: The caller extracts the correct flag bits and chooses the proper Replace permission; the end-to-end oracle checks ordinary region codes, not every malformed flag combination.
gaps: Prove field extraction and caller permission propagation, all reserved-code errors and refinement/colour-specific restrictions.

requirements.title: Gate a direct region's nondefault operator on the page override permission
requirements.scope_of_formal_result: Success implies override permission, equal operators or the refinement exception; an error implies all three alternatives fail.
assumptions: The caller must supply correct page/region operators and the refinement Boolean; the direct-region test sets refinement false.
gaps: Prove flag propagation, complete acceptance and typed errors; separately review and prove every special refinement operator rule.

requirements.title: Reject a coloured-page declaration with the profile's typed unsupported error
